description_en: A group of stone memorial pillars and a stūpa from the 13th-15th century.The artefacts are found on a paved longitudinal terrace in the village of Koṭgāũ. Koṭgāũ is located 300 meters south-east of Kālikoṭ Bajār the settlement that gave its name to the Kalikoṭ district. On the hill east of Koṭgāũ is the settlement of Gelā.Six memorial pillars are placed throughout the area. Elements of medieval monuments are also found erected as if they were memorial pillars. In the south-eastern part is a small temple-like structure and a small stūpa (007).The pillars were all decorated and inscribed. They are nevertheless too eroded to provide information on the dates and contexts of installation. Stone pillars were erected throughout the Karnali Basin from the 13th to the 17th century. They are installed to honor the memory of deceased persons, mostly warriors. It is possible to situate the Koṭgāũ pillars between the 13th and the 15th century on the basis of their various shapes (seeAndolfatto 2019).According to local informants the stūpa (007) was dismantled by Maoists during the Civil War. The culprits were probaly looking for treasures to loot. The monument has been rebuilt since then. Its style, with receeding steps topped by a square volume surmounted by another level of receeding steps, is the same as that of other stūpas found in the Jumla and Dailekh district. The Śrīḍhuskā Stūpa (JUM0110) bears an inscription readingOṃ maṇi padme hūṃ, Avalokiteśvara's mantra, in Rañjana script. The epigraphy is identical to the one seen on the same mantra inscribed on Dullu's Kīrtikhambā (DLK0260), the Patharnauli reservoir (DLK0160). Both monuments were built in the 1350's, during the rule of king Pṛthvīmalla (r. 1338-1358) (Andolfatto 2019, p. 96;Pant 2009, 301). It is thus likely that the Śrīḍhuskā Stūpa, as well as the stūpa in Koṭgāũ were built around the same period.
monument_assessment: Demolition/Dismantling, Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. 2019. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne Université.
